title: Hostinger Review - The Good and Bad (Updated for 2026)
headings: Hostinger: The Good and The Bad
text: Hostinger has come a long way since it first launched as a free web hosting service 15+ years ago. Today, it’s one of the most recognized names in web hosting—offering affordable plans, a high-quality experience, and other perks for website owners. Whether you’re launching a new site from scratch or switching providers, you can use this in-depth review to see if Hostinger is right for you (hint: it probably is ). Choosing a quality web hosting service is crucial. Your web host has a direct impact on things like uptime, page loading speed, and other performance metrics that impact the end-user experience. Moreso, customer service, scalability, and ease of use impact your experience as the website owner. We’ve used dozens of hosts ourselves over the years and performed thorough testing with just about every hosting provider out there. And one thing we can say for sure is that Hostinger offers an excellent balance of price, performance, support, usability, and long-term scalability. That’s ultimately why it’s what we recommend for most new websites. Eventually, you’ll want to switch to something more powerful, like WP Engine. But that won’t be necessary for a long time. Hostinger plans can be as low as $1.99 per month on the longest-term deals, which is one of the most affordable options you’ll find from a hosting service so reputable. But don’t let that price fool you. It doesn’t feel cheap. See our full list of the best cheap hosting providers if you want to weigh all your options. Hostinger: The Good and The Bad Like any product on the market, there are pros and cons to choosing Hostinger as your websites’ web host. We want to call out a few of the key elements that work in Hostinger’s favor and a couple potential drawbacks, so you get the full story on whether they’re the best choice for you. The Good Fast load times : If a visitor comes to your website and has to wait for things to load, they won’t stick around. In fact, many people aren’t willing to wait for more than a couple of seconds for a site to load. The good news is that Hostinger delivers consistently fast speeds for a shared hosting service. And we’re not just going off of what they tell everyone on their webpage copy, we’ve tested their shared hosting, VPS hosting , and WordPress hosting ourselves. We experienced loading times around 500 ms across the board (with VPS hosting being slightly faster). LiteSpeed web servers: These are the key behind Hostinger’s impressive speed. The use of LiteSpeed allows Hostinger to deploy its custom hPanel without sacrificing performance. It’s much faster than Apache web servers used by most cheap shared hosting providers. Additionally, LSWS uses a cache to store copies of your web pages, allowing visitors to load everything faster. Global data centers: Hostinger maintains data centers across the globe, including North America, South America, and multiple locations throughout Europe and Asia (US, UK, France, Germany, Netherlands, Lithuania, India, Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Brazil). If you leverage Hostinger’s CDN (included with Business and up), your website will use whatever location’s closest to the visitor to keep load times as fast as possible. But the main advantages of multiple data centers are that you can choose the one closest to your audience and a different data center can take over if the one hosting your site experiences an outage. It’s very affordable : Not only do you get blazing fast site speeds, but you’ll also pay rock-bottom prices. Hostinger’s entry-level plan can be under $2 per month on the longest-term promos, and its higher shared tiers are still budget-friendly for the features you get. Cloud plans start at $6.99 per month, and VPS starts at $4.99 per month. Feature-rich: Despite the low price tag, you get backups, free WordPress tools, a website builder, AI capabilities (including an AI Agent for WordPress), malware scanning, a web firewall, a CDN on higher tiers, and more. Like we said, Hostinger certainly doesn’t feel cheap. Free domain for the first year : With annual plans, you’ll get a free domain name for the first year. It comes preconfigured so you don’t have to do any of the technical, behind-the-scenes work to get started, and eligible domains include free WHOIS privacy protection. Complimentary AI-powered website builder : Hostinger offers one of the better website builders on the market—included for free with every plan. Whether you need a basic company website or fully-functional online store, it’s easy to use even if you have zero technical experience. There are more than 100 templates you can start with–or you can use the AI site builder to whip up a customized site in a matter of minutes. It’s easy to get started : Hostinger is really easy to use, especially when getting everything set up. The hosting service’s clean interface, guided setup, and user-friendly dashboard makes it easy for first-timers; you don’t need to take a class on this hosting service to use it. One-click installs: Though it’s simple, Hostinger doesn’t skimp on powerful tools. For example, Hostinger offers an Auto Installer feature that greatly simplifies the process of installing apps. It seriously takes one click and you can have a brand new WordPress, Drupal, WooCommerce, or PrestaShop site ready to go. No messing with code or going through lengthy installation processes to get going. Easy site migrations: Hostinger will handle all the technical details of moving an existing website to their hosting services. All you have to do is initiate a website migration, provide a few details, and you’re good to go. hPanel is very user-friendly: hPanel is an entirely custom website control panel that puts cPanel’s ease of use to shame. Everything’s designed well, laid out in a manner that makes sense, and incredibly easy to navigate. You won’t have to guess where things are, either. We found it to be a refreshingly well-done cPanel alternative you won’t get from any other host. Strong customer service: While Hostinger’s support wasn’t the fastest, every rep we talked to provided clear answers. We walked away from every interaction knowing exactly what to do. They even provided annotated screenshots showing us where to click. This level of detail is something we didn’t experience from any other budget hosting service. Moneyback guarantee: Not happy with your Hostinger purchase? No problem. You have 30 days to try it out and get your money back if your experience is not all you were hoping for. However, be sure to note that redemption fees, domain name renewals, and privacy protection are not part of the guarantee. The Bad No phone support: Hostinger offers a series of tutorials, blog posts, and knowledge base articles to help you if you need it. There’s also Hostinger Academy, which is a series of tutorials on YouTube. As helpful as these items are, they aren’t the same as a phone call to walk you through things when you are experiencing some frustration. Unfortunately, the only ways to get in touch with customer support are via a live chat and email or ticket, both of which are available 24/7. Uptime can dip on lower-tier shared plans: During earlier testing, we had a few instances where our site was down for a few minutes at a time—this is pretty normal for shared hosting. More recent tests showed Hostinger hovering around 99.9%+ uptime for shared and WordPress hosting, and its VPS hosting performed even better over long windows. If absolute uptime is critical, you’ll still want to spring for cloud or VPS. No dedicated servers: If a VPS server isn’t enough for you, you’ll have to switch to a different host as Hostinger doesn’t offer dedicated servers. For developers who want full control without paying for bare metal, Hostinger’s unmanaged KVM VPS plans include full root access and a dedicated IP, which covers most advanced use cases. If you’re a developer who specifically needs a dedicated, bare-metal environment, this is a sign Hostinger isn’t right for you. Hostinger Pricing and Options Hostinger has a number of different packages for you to choose from. Each one offers unique things that are suited for specific needs. If you’re on a super tight budget, free plans that used to be available via 000webhost have been discontinued. We don’t recommend free hosting for serious projects anyway. Here’s a closer look at Hostinger’s plans and pricing. Hostinger Premium This is Hostinger’s cheapest hosting plan. On the longest-term deals, it can be as low as $1.99 per month. It’s designed for getting a site online quickly without paying for features you don’t need. You’ll be able to host up to three websites with 20 GB of SSD storage, unlimited bandwidth, and a free SSL certificate. You’ll also get a free domain for the first year on annual terms, and that typically includes WHOIS privacy protection for eligible extensions—keeping your private information private and saving you an extra annual fee you’d otherwise pay elsewhere. While you do have to pay for 48 months in advance to get the best price, you’ll still end up paying well under $150 out of pocket today on the biggest promos. Hostinger Business If you’re looking to level up your plan, then Hostinger’s Business option may be right for you. With this plan you get everything included in the Premium plan, plus daily and on-demand backups, more resources to handle higher traffic, NVMe storage, and more builder and WordPress tools that make it easier to grow. Pricing for the Business plan can be as low as $2.99 per month on a long-term term, and goes up to $16.99 per month at renewal. Cloud Hosting If you’re considering cloud hosting vs. traditional shared hosting, take a look at Hostinger’s offerings . Instead of your site being hosted on a single server, it is hosted in the cloud, which allows for more flexibility and easier scalability. You can choose from: Cloud Startup – Starts at $6.99 per month Cloud Professional – Starts at $15.99 per month Cloud Enterprise – Starts at $29.99 per month They all come with the same core features; the main differences are storage, processing, and computing power. Cloud plans also add a dedicated IP, priority support, and short-term power boosts to handle traffic spikes. VPS Hosting If you need more control and more processing power, Hostinger’s VPS hosting plans are a great upgrade from shared hosting. Every VPS plan comes with the same features, including weekly backups, full root access, malware scanning, dedicated IP, and AI assistant. The only difference is you’re getting more computing power, memory, disk space, and bandwidth at each tier. Hostinger offers four VPS hosting plans to chose from, including: KVM 1 – Starts at $4.99 per month KVM 2 – Starts at $6.99 per month KVM 4 – Starts at $9.99 per month KVM 8 – Starts at $19.99 per month The KVM 1 plan starts with 4 GB of RAM, 50 GB of storage, and 4 TB of bandwidth, while the KVM 8 plan scales up to 32 GB of RAM, 400 GB of storage, and 32 TB of bandwidth. Minecraft Hosting Hostinger offers a unique hosting service that many of its competitors don’t: Minecraft server hosting geared towards gamers. Pricing typically starts around $5.49 per month on a two-year term and scales up for higher-resource servers depending on the plan you choose. With this service, you can install your own game mods, along with many other things. Expanding Your Hostinger Knowledge Is Hostinger good for web hosting? Hostinger is the best web hosting provider on the market today. It’s perfect for new users seeking a simple and affordable way to launch a new website. From registering a new domain to hosting your website, Hostinger has everything you need to get started. Hostinger has shared web hosting plans, VPS hosting plans, cloud hosting, and WordPress hosting options to choose from. Is Hostinger reliable? Hostinger is a reliable web hosting provider. They provide fast loading times and high uptime rates to ensure your site visitors can access your site whenever they need to. Hostinger also offers helpful and friendly customer support available 24/7. So if you have any questions or need help, you can rely on Hostinger to be there for you. You can also rely on Hostinger to help keep your site secure. Hostinger powers millions of websites and domain registrations worldwide. Plus, services are backed by a 30-day money-back guarantee. Does Hostinger offer any special promotions? New customers can unlock Hostinger’s special promotion of up to 85% off web hosting services and up to three months free. You’ll also get a free domain name for one year with the purchase of any web hosting plan. How does Hostinger compare to other web hosting providers? Compared to other web hosting providers, Hostinger offers the best value for reliability, performance, and user experience. It’s tough to find a better deal from such a reliable and reputable hosting provider. While Hostinger’s page-loading speeds and uptime rates aren’t necessarily leading the pack, they’re still solid enough to accommodate new websites—especially low-traffic sites that are on a budget. With that said, Hostinger’s ease of use is unmatched compared to its competitors. How do I transfer my website to Hostinger? To transfer your website to Hostinger, the first thing you need to do is sign up for Hostinger and select a plan . You can request a free migration service during initial sign-up, or you can select the Migrate Website option from your Profile drop-down menu. Click the Add Request button to transfer your website to Hostinger for free. WordPress migrations are automated and usually complete within 24 hours (and can take up to 48 hours) to complete. Is Hostinger good for domain registration? Hostinger is good for domain registration if you’re creating a new website and want to bundle your domain name with your hosting plan. Hostinger simplifies this process by offering both services under one roof, and you’ll even get a free domain name for your first year. But if you’re planning to use another web hosting provider, you may want to look elsewhere. There are better options on the market for things like bulk domain purchases and extended registrations. Refer to our list of the best domain registrars for Hostinger alternatives. Is Hostinger good for cloud hosting? Hostinger is one of the best cloud web hosting services on the market. It’s ideal for websites seeking an upgrade from entry-level shared plans without breaking the bank. Hostinger provides the perfect balance of speed, performance, and ease of use—making it harder to find a better value in the cloud hosting space. Whether you’re leveling up from a shared plan, switching from another provider, or launching a new site, Hostinger’s cloud hosting plans are versatile enough for a wide range of use cases. Is Hostinger or HostGator better? Hostinger is better than HostGator for most web hosting needs. Hostinger performs better in almost every category. However, HostGator is a reputable hosting provider, too. You really can’t go wrong with either.

The cracks show on renewal day and during VPS upgrades, where pricing jumps 3–4× and CPU resources can feel oversold. TL;DR Yes for first-year buyers on a tight budget. No for anyone running production workloads, anyone who hates surprise renewal hikes, or anyone needing dedicated VPS resources at the entry tier. Care most about price for the first 12–24 months. Run a small WordPress blog, portfolio, or a low-traffic business site. Want one provider for hosting + domain + email + AI website builder. Look elsewhere if you: Run a production workload that can't tolerate noisy-neighbor CPU. Need predictable pricing past month 12. Want full root access, custom kernels, or specific Docker setups on the entry VPS tier. Need 24/7 expert-tier support regardless of plan. Hostinger product lineup, plan by plan Hostinger covers most of the small-business hosting stack. Here's what each product looks like in 2026. Web Hosting (shared) The flagship product. Four tiers, all on LiteSpeed servers with hPanel. Plan Intro price Renewal Sites Best for Premium ~$2.49/mo ~$8.99/mo 25 Most personal sites Business ~$3.99/mo ~$11.99/mo 100 Small business + light commerce Cloud Startup ~$8.99/mo ~$19.99/mo 100 Higher-traffic WP / WooCommerce Cloud Professional ~$15.99/mo ~$29.99/mo 300 Agencies, ~200K visits/mo What's good: LiteSpeed Web Server + LSCache, free SSL, free email on most tiers, weekly backups (daily on higher plans), AI website builder included. What's not: Resources are clearly shared, "Cloud" plans are still on shared infrastructure (not true cloud VMs), and the intro-vs-renewal gap is severe. Managed WordPress Hosting Hostinger's managed WordPress sits on the same shared infrastructure as web hosting, with LiteSpeed Cache pre-configured, automatic WordPress core updates, and an AI website builder. For a small WordPress site, it works well — sub-second TTFB on cached pages and an opinionated dashboard make it beginner-friendly. For a busy WooCommerce store or membership site, the shared resources start to bite. If a managed environment matters more than rock-bottom pricing, alternatives like Kinsta, WP Engine, or a managed VPS layer (such as BearHost's managed VPS option ) deliver more headroom. BearHost's WordPress hosting is the flat-renewal comparison point. WooCommerce Hosting Hostinger markets a dedicated WooCommerce tier built on the Business or Cloud Startup plans, with WooCommerce pre-installed and storefront templates available. Performance is competent up to a few hundred SKUs and modest traffic. Above that, the underlying shared infrastructure becomes the bottleneck. VPS Hosting This is where Hostinger's weakest plans live. KVM 1 starts at ~$5.99/mo intro for 1 vCPU / 4GB RAM / 50GB NVMe, but the lower tiers share CPU cycles broadly. Dedicated-vCPU performance only appears on higher tiers. The control panel is clean and the OS choices are reasonable (Ubuntu, Debian, AlmaLinux, plus app templates). What's missing: full 24/7 expert-tier support for VPS troubleshooting on the cheapest plans, and the renewal pricing remains the same 2–3× pattern as the shared tier. If you've outgrown a shared plan and want predictable VPS pricing with dedicated resources from the entry tier, BearHost VPS starts at $5.49/mo with KVM dedicated cores and no renewal hike — one option of several covered in the alternatives section below. Cloud Hosting The "Cloud" line is marketed as a step up from shared but it's still managed multi-tenant infrastructure, not true VMs. You get dedicated resource caps per plan, isolated IP, daily backups, and CloudLinux. For a serious traffic site, this is the sweet spot in Hostinger's lineup before having to move to VPS. Email Hosting Hostinger's email is free on most web hosting plans (limits apply) and available standalone via Hostinger Mail (~$0.99/mo per inbox) or Google Workspace integration. Decent UX, basic features. Power users will outgrow it quickly. Domain Registration Domains are cheap on first-year promos (often $1 for .com) and renewed at standard market rates ($14.99 for .com in 2026). Whois privacy is free. The domain panel is integrated tightly with hosting, which is convenient if you want everything in one place. Hostinger pricing — the renewal reality QUICK ANSWER Hostinger's first-year value is real. Its five-year value is closer to industry average — sometimes worse than competitors that don't run the same intro-vs-renewal gap. Most ranking-competitive reviews (including the affiliate-driven ones) lead with the $2.49/month headline price. The honest version: that price requires a four-year commitment, and renewals push the monthly cost to $8.99–$11.99 depending on plan. The full Hostinger pricing breakdown maps every plan's intro price, renewal rate, and 5-year total . Plan 48-mo total (intro) 12-mo renewal 5-year total Premium ~$120 (4 yr) ~$108/yr ~$228 Business ~$192 (4 yr) ~$144/yr ~$336 Cloud Startup ~$432 (4 yr) ~$240/yr ~$672 Hostinger performance — what aggregated benchmarks show Based on publicly available uptime monitoring, third-party benchmark databases, and Hostinger's own published SLAs: Uptime: typically 99.95–99.99% on shared and managed WordPress, in line with industry leaders. TTFB (cached page): ~150–400ms depending on data center region, helped by LiteSpeed + LSCache. TTFB (uncached, dynamic): ~600ms–1.2s on entry tiers, improves on Cloud and VPS. Network: 1Gbps standard on VPS, fast routing to major peering points. For a typical small business WordPress site, this is enough. For high-traffic or commerce workloads, you'll want at least Cloud Startup or a dedicated-CPU VPS — at which point you should also be price-comparing against alternatives. Hostinger customer support Live chat 24/7 on paid plans. Email/ticket support across all plans. No phone support. Tier-1 chat agents handle most queries; complex issues escalate slowly. Quality varies by plan and time of day. Premium and Business users typically report acceptable response times. VPS users on the entry tier report longer queues for technical troubleshooting — a known weak point that affiliate reviews often soften. Hostinger security and backups Free SSL across all plans (Let's Encrypt). Weekly backups on Premium; daily on Business and above. DDoS protection at the infrastructure level. Hostinger Monarx and basic WAF on managed plans. Two-factor authentication for the account panel. Solid for a host at this price point. Not industry-leading, but no glaring gaps. Hostinger pros and cons Pros Cons + Among the cheapest intro pricing in the industry − Renewal pricing 3–4× the intro rate + hPanel is one of the most beginner-friendly control panels − "Cloud" hosting isn't true cloud VMs + LiteSpeed + LSCache deliver fast cached TTFB − VPS lower tiers oversold on CPU + AI website builder works for non-designers − No phone support + Free SSL, free email, free CDN on most plans − Tier-1 chat handles most VPS troubleshooting + 30-day money-back guarantee − Multi-year commitment required for headline price Hostinger alternatives worth comparing If Hostinger's renewal pricing, VPS oversell, or support tier-gating is a problem for you, three alternatives consistently come up in the same searches: SiteGround — pricier but stronger support and more transparent renewal pricing. Cloudways — managed cloud hosting on DigitalOcean / Vultr / AWS infrastructure; mid-priced, developer-friendly. BearHost — KVM VPS from $5.49/mo with NVMe SSD, dedicated resources from the entry tier, and 24/7 human support. No renewal hike. See BearHost VPS or Switch from Hostinger for free migration help. It's not the host that automatically wins year two or year five. If you understand the renewal economics, accept the entry-tier VPS limitations, and just need a simple, affordable home for a small site, Hostinger is hard to beat. text: Hostinger offers excellent web hosting for both beginners and advanced users seeking a user-friendly site-building experience. I liked its intuitive website and server management tools, which made it easy to get started. You can enjoy excellent upfront savings, but you’ll need to lock into a four-year contract to access the best introductory rates on most plans. As such, I only recommend Hostinger if you’re confident you’ll be running your website long-term. To test Hostinger, I signed up for a plan, assessed its registration process, benchmarked server performance, measured uptime, scrutinized plans to determine value and contacted customer support to evaluate its effectiveness. Overall, I found Hostinger an easy-to-use web host with exceptional initial value. I also liked its reliable uptime. However, Hostinger’s inconsistent site speeds without optimization tools and unreliable human customer service mean it might not work for large, complex websites or folks who need regular human-assisted troubleshooting. While I’ve only needed to contact customer support a handful of times in my 20 years of building websites, you may want to avoid Hostinger if you expect to need advanced customer support. More from CNET James Martin/CNET Hostinger 7.8 See at Hostinger Pros & Cons Introductory discounts can provide significant long-term savings Beginner-friendly site and server management tools, including specialized WordPress tools Excellent tutorials and knowledge base for building your website and addressing simple problem Best possible introductory pricing requires a four-year commitment upfront Default server speed without optimization tools is highly variable, especially on mobile Accessing human support for complex issues is difficult Value: Solid prices for long-term hosting Key takeaway: Hostinger provides good value for anyone seeking long-term shared, WordPress or WooCommerce hosting to build small websites. People building larger websites or expecting significant traffic — like big content sites or large companies — can get good deals on cloud hosting. Hosting type Best for Starting price Shared hosting For-fun hobby sites, blogs or professional portfolios using a system other than WordPress $12 per month, $48 for the first year, $84 for the first two years or $144 for the first four years (one-, two- and four-year plans renew at $132 a year) WordPress hosting For-fun hobby sites, blogs or professional portfolios built on WordPress $12 a month, $48 for the first year (renews at $132 a year), $84 for the first two years (renews at $264 total for two years) or $144 for the first four years (renews at $528 total for four years) WooCommerce hosting Small-to-medium-sized online stores $19 a month, $60 for the first year (renews at $204), $108 total for the first two years (renews at $408 total for two years) or $192 total for the first four years (renews at $816 total for four years) Cloud hosting High-traffic websites and large online stores $28 a month, $120 for the first year (renews at $312 a year), $216 for the first two years (renews at $624 total for two years) or $384 total for the first four years (renews at $1,248 total for four years) VPS hosting High-traffic websites hosted by companies with the resources for hiring a dedicated system admin $10 for the first month (renews at $19.49 a month), $84 for the first year (renews at $156 a year) or $156 for total for the first two years (renews at $288 total for two years) Hostinger’s pricing for most plans is similar to top rivals like SiteGround and Ionos , but the four-year contract period for the introductory price on shared and WordPress hosting can result in long-term savings over similar plans from other top companies. Shared hosting and WordPress hosting Shared hosting and WordPress hosting are ideal for most blogs , professional portfolios and hobby sites thanks to their simple setup and low cost . Hostinger’s prices are pretty average, sitting between other top web hosts like Ionos and SiteGround. Hostinger’s best deals are for a four-year plan, so you’ll pay more up front than you would for a similarly priced one-year contract from a company like SiteGround, but you’ll get considerable savings over the long term. For shared and WordPress hosting, the best-value plan costs $144 for the first four years (renewing at $528 total for the next four years), or you can pay $48 for a one-year contract (renewing at $132 for the next year). There are also monthly and two-year plans, but the monthly tier is expensive, and tough to recommend unless you only need short-term web hosting. Likewise, the two-year plan is decent, but you get better value with the four-year option if you can stomach the commitment. Shared hosting and WordPress hosting split server resources (like CPU and RAM) between numerous websites, with the main difference being that WordPress hosting includes auto-updates to the CMS and other specialized tools for the popular content management system, which powers 41.1% of all websites . Shared servers let companies keep prices low, but large websites, or those expecting rapid growth, may want more advanced options like VPS or cloud hosting. WooCommerce hosting WooCommerce hosting is ideal for anyone looking to build an online store, with more extensive storage and servers optimized for WooCommerce (a popular store-building plugin for WordPress). Prices are similar to comparable plans from competitors like SiteGround and Ionos (though Ionos’s introductory discount isn’t as steep). A four-year plan gives you the best initial value — $192 for the first four years, renewing at $816 for the next four — but can be a big commitment. You can opt for a one-year plan priced at $60 (renewing at $204 annually) to receive more moderate savings without the time commitment. Alternatively, you can pick a monthly or two-year plan. VPS and cloud hosting Hostinger offers VPS and cloud hosting for high-traffic websites like popular online stores. The best-value VPS hosting plan starts at $156 total for the first two years (renewing at $288 total for two years), or you can buy a one-year plan for $84 (renewing at $288 annually). There’s also a monthly plan for maximum flexibility, but it’s expensive and tough to recommend. Entry-level VPS plans are fully unmanaged , meaning you’ll need to configure and maintain the server or hire someone else to do it. Buying a managed VPS server from a company like DreamHost may be cheaper compared to Hostinger’s pricier AI-managed VPS plans. Hostinger’s cloud hosting is more expensive — the best-value plan costs $384 for the first four years, which works out to $8 a month, paid upfront (renewing at $1,248 total for the next four years) — but its servers are fully managed. As such, it’s a good deal when compared to more expensive managed cloud hosting plans from companies like ScalaHosting. If you don’t want to lock in for four years, you can buy a one-year plan for $120 (renews at $316). Ease of use: Perfect for first-time website owners Key takeaway: Hostinger’s purchase process, account management and website creation tools are highly intuitive, with quick access to numerous tutorials if you get stuck. Whether you’re new to web hosting or you’re simply looking for a quick, easy way to set up your website, Hostinger’s tools have you covered. I bought a shared hosting plan from Hostinger and built a basic WordPress test site. I had a few minor complaints — notably the confusing numbers on Hostinger’s pricing page — but the experience was overwhelmingly straightforward and pleasant. A mostly streamlined purchase process Hostinger’s checkout process is easy, but sneaky marketing tactics can make you think you’re getting a bigger discount than you actually are. Like most web hosts (and other services like VPNs ), Hostinger displays a crossed-out “regular” rate above its more prominent introductory price. However, that “regular” price isn’t the renewal cost — the true renewal rate is listed in small text underneath the introductory rate and is generally lower than the “regular” price. It feels somewhat misleading, making the discount less significant than you might initially think. Thankfully, the checkout process is simple. A drop-down menu lets you select different contract lengths, which can be helpful if you don’t want to lock in for four years. A domain search bar lets you claim a domain through Hostinger, though I prefer buying domains through a dedicated registrar . Hostinger includes one upsell — for email hosting — but this can easily be ignored, letting you complete your purchase in a couple of minutes. Account management is intuitive Hostinger’s account management dashboard is easy for even first-time website owners to navigate. Areas like website, domain and email management are easily accessed through the left-hand toolbar. Account and billing management are found in a dropdown menu accessed via the user icon in the top-right corner. I’d like to see these in the main toolbar, but many websites — including the ubiquitous Google — place account settings in a similar menu, so it’s still intuitive for many internet users. Website and server management Screenshot by Dianna Gunn/CNET Hostinger offers quick and easy options for new website creation, simple (just a few clicks) site migration and having someone build your site. You’ll then get to choose between vibe coding, using the drag-and-drop website builder or creating a WordPress site. I chose WordPress and found the setup process simple and pleasant. Hostinger’s WordPress onboarding plugin is excellent. It provides a checklist and tutorials (including video tutorials) for various website-building tasks. The option to quick-install plugins is especially handy, as it includes high-quality plugins for SEO and spam filtering. However, I wish the checklist included links for making your first page and blog post. Additional tabs of Hostinger’s onboarding plugin provide immediate access to Hostinger’s AI tools. This includes Hostinger Reach, an AI-based email marketing service, though you’ll need to buy it through a separate subscription before you can use it. Server management is conducted through Hostinger’s proprietary hPanel, which is both more aesthetically pleasing and more straightforward than the industry-standard cPanel. I especially appreciate the domain checklist on individual domain pages, which provides helpful guidance for first-time website owners. However, most free website migration services from web hosting companies rely on cPanel, so this can make it harder to transfer your site to a new web host if you decide to switch. Performance: Reliable uptime, inconsistent site speed Key takeaway: Hostinger’s servers offer reliable uptime comparable to many other web hosts, but its server speeds are lacking without optimization tools enabled, especially for people using mobile devices. You’ll want to take additional measures to improve site speed if you’re using Hostinger. To succeed, a website needs to have fast, reliable performance. I spent a week tracking two performance metrics for my Hostinger test site: Uptime: The percentage of time your website spends online and accessible to the public. Visitors who find your website down may be more likely to go elsewhere, making it essential to seek a host with a high (99.9% or above) uptime. Site speed: The number of seconds your site takes to load. Experts recommend aiming for a site speed under two seconds, as conversion rates drop by 1% to 3% per additional 100ms after the 2-second mark. My Hostinger site had solid uptime during my tests, with only one 2-minute downtime incident. Server speeds were mostly fast with optimization tools enabled, but underwhelming without performance-enhancing features toggled on. Uptime was great Hostinger offers the industry-standard 99.9% uptime guarantee, meaning your site shouldn’t go down for more than 10 minutes per week due to server issues. I used Better Stack to monitor my test site’s uptime for one week, and it experienced just 2 minutes of downtime, suggesting that Hostinger lives up to its guarantee and may even exceed it. Site speed was great with optimization tools, but underwhelming without I created a simple website and used WebPageTest to simulate loading my site on desktop and mobile from various locations around the globe over five days, with the following averages: Optimized vs. unoptimized Web page type US UK Germany India Dubai Australia Global Unoptimized Mobile 0.97 1.27 1.40 2.69 2.05 2.3 1.78 Unoptimized Desktop 4.57 4.45 4.62 4.51 4.74 5.34 5.34 Optimized Desktop 1.05 1.27 1.33 2.74 2.19 2.48 1.84 Optimized Mobile 2.1 2.68 2.74 3.05 4.01 3.94 3.08 Together, the global desktop and mobile averages using Hostinger’s default settings result in an overall average of 3.56 seconds — much higher than the recommended 2-second maximum. Enabling Hostinger’s speed-enhancing server-side caching and CDN reduced this average to 2.46 seconds, better than the current default server speed but not as good as the 2.34 second average I experienced in my 2024 Hostinger tests. Site speed was particularly poor outside of the US and Europe, with Australia showing the worst loading times. Mobile speed was also much longer than desktop speed, which is concerning since 64.35% of all internet traffic comes from mobile devices . Loading times are often slower internationally and on mobile devices, but these discrepancies were more significant than I expected based on tests I conducted in 2024. Notably, enabling speed-enhancing features, like server-side caching and a CDN, for one day resulted in significantly faster speeds. These tools brought the desktop average under the recommended 2-second maximum. Mobile speed improved too, but slow loading times in India, Dubai and Australia kept the mobile average over three seconds, resulting in a combined average of 2.46 seconds. My website was hosted on a US server. If your primary audience is outside the US, you may be able to improve loading times for them by choosing a data center in another location, as their devices won’t be required to draw data all the way across the globe. You can also take other steps to improve your site speed . Performance tools may be able to compensate for sluggish server speeds Every Hostinger WordPress install includes both proprietary caching and the LiteSpeed Cache plugin, which can improve your site speed by storing static information (data that isn’t frequently changed, like your home page) in a special high-speed storage layer. LiteSpeed can further improve site speed through image and page optimization techniques, such as code minification. Certain Hostinger plans include a proprietary CDN, or content delivery network, which stores website data in a network of interconnected servers worldwide. This can improve site speed by letting a visitor’s devices pull website data from a location close to them rather than one across the globe. Security: Above average, but it could still be better Key takeaway: Hostinger plans include the core security features needed to safely run a website, plus a couple of extras — but its lack of automated daily backups is disappointing. Every Hostinger plan includes three essential layers of security for encrypting data transmission, guarding against malware and protecting against malicious traffic: SSL certification: Encrypts data sent to and from your website, such as email addresses submitted through a contact form. Browsers and VPNs consider SSL certification a key safety signal and may not allow you to open sites without it. SSL certification is also a key Google ranking factor . Firewall software: Scans website traffic, identifies and attempts to block malware and malicious traffic. You can think of it as the website equivalent of an HVAC filter, allowing good stuff into your space while keeping bad stuff out. DDoS protection: Blocks distributed denial of service attacks, which flood websites with malicious traffic to overwhelm web servers and cause shutdowns. Most web hosts – including top companies such as Ionos and AccuWeb – offer these essential features. Hostinger takes security a step further with a malware scanner for finding threats that get past the firewall, which you don’t always get from other hosts. Additionally, the Secure Access Manager lets you give collaborators limited access to your hosting account, which can be helpful if you want someone to assist you with specific aspects of server or site management. Secure Access Manager could be helpful for agencies or remote teams with multiple website administrators. Unfortunately, Hostinger restricts automated daily backups to its higher-tier plans, with the entry-level plan limited to weekly backups. You’ll have to use a separate backup solution to get more frequent backups if you’re on the lowest-tier plan — or use a different web host, like SiteGround, that bundles daily automated backups into every hosting package. Customer service: Great self-serve support and a well-trained AI support bot, but poor human support Key takeaway: Hostinger provides excellent tutorials through its knowledge base and learning lab, but its live support is strongly AI-focused. I experienced significant difficulties attempting to speak with a human, leaving me concerned that people with more serious issues may be unable to get the help they need. To gauge its troubleshooting capabilities, I explored Hostinger’s self-serve tutorials and tested its 24/7 live chat for both AI and human support. Hostinger also has a public-facing support email, but it recommends only using this if you can’t access your account or you’re not yet using Hostinger and you have questions the customer-facing bot can’t answer. As such, I did not test email support. Hostinger knowledge base and tutorials Hostinger’s knowledge base is difficult to find. I found a “Learning Lab” link in the account menu, but quickly realized this wasn’t the knowledge base — and the actual knowledge base was only accessible through a link in the footer of the public-facing site. This problem is as unusual as it is frustrating: None of the other hosts I’ve tested failed to include a knowledge base link in the account area. Once I found it, however, the knowledge base proved extremely useful. There are extensive tutorials on every aspect of building your site, with a mix of beginner-friendly articles, image-based tutorials and videos. I was also impressed by the learning lab, which goes beyond the standard knowledge base fare with advanced guides on creating specific types of blogs, online stores and other websites. Direct communication (email, live chat, phone, social media) Hostinger offers 24/7 customer support through its AI bot, Kodee. Theoretically, Hostinger also provides 24/7 live chat support from human agents, but I never managed to speak to a person. Unlike the knowledge base, Kodee’s easy to find — there’s a prominent box for asking questions on the account dashboard homepage, an “Ask AI” button in the top bar and a pop-up encouraging you to ask Kodee for help when you use the search function. Kodee’s well-trained, too, near-instantly pulling knowledge base answers to most simple questions. Unfortunately, I had to ask to speak to a person twice before Kodee directed me to human support. My question was then “sent for human review,” and I received a boilerplate response about 5 minutes later. When I asked a follow-up question, Kodee responded. I was unable to convince the bot to let me have a proper conversation with a person, and the boilerplate text in my “human-reviewed” response made me wonder whether a human had really looked at my case. Reputation Hostinger has a Trustpilot ranking of 4.7 out of 5 based on an impressive 71,000 reviews, with the reviews themselves suggesting that most people enjoy Hostinger for the same reasons I did — intuitive site-building tools, excellent server management options and comprehensive tutorials. However, there are over 5,000 negative reviews, mostly citing the same issues I experienced with customer service. This suggests that Hostinger’s customer support is inconsistent. Hostinger is a solid web host for most folks, but its sluggish server speeds and customer service issues may hold it back Hostinger’s beginner-friendly website management tools and impressive long-term discounts make it an attractive choice for anyone seeking a simple hosting experience for a casual website like a for-fun blog or small businesses with a tight budget. Default server speed isn’t great, but you can improve it by enabling proprietary speed-boosting and optimization tools. Poor customer support may be off-putting for some people if they expect to need regular human-assisted troubleshooting. But the self-serve solutions are comprehensive, and those with simple websites may be unlikely to need regular direct support. Hostinger offers excellent prices on its cloud hosting for more advanced websites, like e-commerce sites, large content sites and other bigger operations. However, its lack of human customer support means you may not be able to receive the help you need when running into more advanced issues — which can be majorly detrimental if you rely on your site for income. You may want to choose a competitor like SiteGround if you’re building a complex website or a website for a large business.
